newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan to sell shares in state bank, power plant.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan to sell shares in state bank, power plant.

text.p: Pakistan's government plans to sell some of its shares in the privatised Muslim Commercial Bank (MCB) and Kot Addu Power Co Ltd (KAPCO), an official said on Tuesday.
Salman Shah, chairman of the Privatisation Commission, told Reuters he would soon ask caretaker Prime Minister Meraj Khalid's cabinet to approve the sale of shares to the public.

"We have some of these shares, and in principle we want to do a flotation and really take the benefits of privatisation to the public. We want to attract a few million new share-holders to invest in stocks," Shah said.
He said the shares would be sold in small packages worth 3,000 to 5,000 rupees that small investors could afford.
The government owns a 24 percent stake in MCB and a 64 percent stake in KAPCO.
